tagline: Up the Susquehanna's east bank, over the dam, down the west.
intro: From Perryville, where Rodgers Tavern stands beside the old ferry crossing and George Washington stopped often, the byway goes up the east bank of the Susquehanna through Port Deposit, crosses the river on top of Conowingo Dam and comes back down the west side by Susquehanna State Park to Havre de Grace. It is 33 miles around.

The lower river ran over rapids and falls, and the towns grew where cargo changed hands. Barges and floated timber came down to Port Deposit and Lapidum, the last deepwater landings, and went on by ship from there.

moments.title: Port Deposit
moments.text: Early 1800s houses below the bluffs along the river, with a 75-step brick and stone stair up from Main Street to a view of four bridges.

moments.title: Conowingo Dam
moments.text: Route 1 runs across the top of the 1928 dam. Below it at Fisherman's Park, bald eagles and great blue herons are often spied along the river.

moments.title: Havre de Grace
moments.text: Missed being the national capital by one vote. After the British raid of 1813 the town made the lieutenant who manned a cannon alone, and his descendants, keepers of Concord Point Lighthouse.
